significance.root_decision: All three relations hold on the whole closed ordered domain, ties and zero entries included. Arguments that use only convexity of x log x (majorization, Schur concavity, Karamata) cannot work, because the inequalities fail when x log x is replaced by x squared, as the source remarks, and the author wrote that these three relations do not yield to the identric-mean technique that proved the others. The proof reduces to a = b by the sign of the derivative in a, uses concavity along a direction that keeps the positive marginals fixed to reduce to five faces of the domain, treats each face by one-variable monotonicity, and on the hardest face uses a weighted gradient bound (log x >= 1 - 1/x with an explicit nonnegative polynomial) followed along the curves A/C^2 = constant. Lean states the mutual information with Mathlib's negMulLog, keeps the joint-entropy term, fixes the direction of the order, and writes the four arrays out explicitly.
significance.caveat: Modest result: about three pages of elementary calculus on a single explicit inequality from a 2012 arXiv preprint with one citing paper; the cross-model reviewer puts 0.60 on a specialist calling it not routine. The source's Definition 4 states the direction of the order once the wrong way round; the convention paragraph and the falsity of the reverse fix the direction used. ProbXiv (HTTP 402) and OpenAlex (429 for one lane) were not fully checked. No second cross-model lane read the finished Lean: root compared the final theorem and every definition with the endpoint the Claude Opus reviewer had written (identical), and the GPT-6.1 Sol final check derived the four arrays from the source independently and spot-checked 240 points.
